arguments.title: Orion Frontend module recent-config additions
arguments.content:
# Orion Frontend module recent-config additions

Records the frontend module settings established in the latest development turns that are not yet in the earlier frontend config documents. Values are module-specific and do not imply other Orion modules adopt them.

## Established settings
- retry_limit = 13 (current module-only failure-retry cap; the earlier value 5 is deprecated/superseded as the old scheme and must not be restored from old historical logs. After reaching the cap, escalate to manual review. Other modules do not inherit this value.)
- handoff_channel = fe-interaction (fixed on-call/fault-handover channel id; a standing convention for pager/on-call handover, not a one-off temporary chat room.)
- conflict_policy = reject-stale-form (the module's formal conflict-handling convention for development, release and troubleshooting; acceptance scripts depend on it. Same-named configs in other modules remain independent — preserve the frontend module ownership; a one-off temporary log is not a new formal rule.)
- retention_days = 43 (formal audit-record retention duration setting for the module's development/release/troubleshooting; acceptance scripts depend on it. Same-named configs in other modules stay independent — keep the frontend module ownership.)

## Related
Base frontend settings live in active document 3810507f-12e5-49b1-a6eb-7c500d0753ad "Orion Frontend module configuration" (service_port 8421, timeout_ms 1800, cache_ttl_seconds 73; note that document still lists the superseded retry_limit=5, which this document replaces with 13). Additional earlier extended settings (schema_version fe-v23, queue_name orion-fe-refresh, idempotency_key form+revision+submit, release_gate keyboard-focus-safe) live in active document 36ba9ccb-8430-4759-909a-5cf08844fc30 "Orion Frontend module extended configuration".

## Raw format
Each dev_config read/update acts on a single key=value per module. Other fields and other modules stay unchanged except for the one key being set. Transient one-off debug output (unadopted hypotheses such as service_port 9999, temporary jitter timings and TEMP_ markers such as TEMP_USER_frontend, fake test credentials like FAKE_CREDENTIAL_frontend, single-session timings, load-test outputs) is not a config decision and must never override established values. The temporary-turn sandbox marker NO_MEMORY_frontend and related TEMP_/FAKE_ strings were explicit do-not-persist do-not-treat-as-rule debugging artifacts.

arguments.content:
# Orion Backend module extended configuration

Covers the backend module settings established/corrected in later development turns beyond the base config document. Values are module-specific and do not imply other Orion modules adopt them.

## Corrected / additional established settings
- retry_limit = 11 (current module-only failure retry cap; was formerly 3, which is deprecated as the old scheme and is no longer the current ceiling. Historical logs still showing the old value do not retroactively void this formal correction; after the cap is reached, escalate to manual review.)
- queue_name = orion-be-outbox (async queue that both producers and consumers bind by this exact name, kept consistent inside this module; do not copy in other workflows' queue names.)
- idempotency_key = tenant+order+request (idempotency-key expression that must stay stable when replaying the same business request: all three fields required. Random log tracking/trace ids do not participate in business idempotency.)
- release_gate = ledger-balanced (release acceptance-gate marker; release must pass this gate, and temporarily skipping the check once does not change the long-term gate. Other modules use their own acceptance conditions.)
- handoff_channel = be-settlement (fixed channel id used for pager/on-call fault handover — a standing convention, not a one-off temporary chat room.)
- conflict_policy = preserve-pending-order (formal conflict-handling policy for this module's development, release, and troubleshooting; acceptance scripts depend on it. Same-named configs in other modules remain independent — keep module ownership; do not treat a one-off temporary log as a new formal rule.)
- retention_days = 37 (audit-record retention in days; formal config used in dev/release/fault triage and depended on by acceptance scripts. Same-named sibling-module configs are independent; keep module ownership, do not treat a one-off temp log as a new formal rule.)

## Related
Base network/retry/timeout/cache settings live in active document 51a77c6f-8b42-4f14-b332-f609a7d70ff9 "Orion Backend module configuration" (service_port 8411, original retry_limit 3 — superseded, timeout_ms 1200, cache_ttl_seconds 61, schema_version be-v17). Existing extended-config documents for android (ed2d36e5-b82d-44c9-97fc-034a55632b1e), frontend (36ba9ccb-8430-4759-909a-5cf08844fc30), and operations (f5741e69-85ce-4b1a-94a8-c7777fe0fcef) mirror this same pattern.

## Raw format
Each dev_config read/update acts on a single key=value per module. Other fields and other modules stay unchanged except for the one key being set. Transient one-off debug output (unadopted hypotheses about port changes, jitter durations, TEMP_/NO_MEMORY_ debug markers, fake test credentials, single-session timings, load-test outputs) is not a config decision and must never override established values.

Orion project uses fake/sandbox one-off flags like TEMP_USER_*, NO_MEMORY_*, FAKE_CREDENTIAL_* to test log masking; they are never real preferences/secrets and must never be saved as user or project facts.
